headline: Maui Planning Commission Approves Lahaina Rebuild, Accepts Mākena EIS

meeting.body: Maui Planning Commission Approves Lahaina Rebuild, Accepts Mākena EIS
meeting.summary: The commission approved a Lahaina fire rebuild with a 10-year shoreline survey rule and accepted the Mākena project's final environmental study.
meeting.recap: The commission heard a request for a coastal-zone permit (special management area permit) to rebuild a Lahaina home destroyed in the August 8, 2023 fire.[[0:02:31]] A testifier opposed the permit, saying the house, pool and landscaping would eventually trap the beach as it moves inland.[[0:44:42]] Commissioners voted to require a state-certified shoreline survey every 10 years, with the first due by August 31, 2036.[[2:54:43]] The commission approved the permit with eight votes.[[2:58:41]] Staff said accepting the EIS does not approve the project, and more permits are still needed.[[3:02:18]] The plan includes 652 homes, 109 of them workforce housing.[[3:21:53]] A testifier asked for a delay until the developer gives a site-specific plan for its system to take salt out of well water.[[4:28:32]] An applicant water expert said the local aquifer is now pumped at about one-third of its sustainable yield.[[4:54:43]] One commissioner said the EIS lacked plans for carbon and waste and would have preferred to defer it.[[6:26:36]] The next meeting is August 25.[[6:29:02]]
decided: Commissioners added a condition requiring a state-certified shoreline survey every 10 years, first due by August 31, 2036.
Commissioners added that the planning department may require shoreline surveys more often.
meeting.next: Parts of the Mākena project still need Land Use Commission, County Council and coastal-zone permit reviews. Phase one of the Mākena project would need a coastal-zone permit that comes back to this commission.
